sub_graphs.title: Bellatrix: Beacon Block Gossip Propagation
sub_graphs.description: Models how beacon blocks with execution payloads are gossiped across the P2P network, including validation and propagation rules

nodes.label: SignedBeaconBlock Received from Peer
nodes.description: A SignedBeaconBlock (with execution payload) has been received via the beacon_block gossip topic

nodes.label: Validate Block Against Consensus Rules
nodes.description: Check the block against consensus-layer validation rules (slot, proposer, signature, parent)

nodes.label: Block Passes Consensus Validation
nodes.description: Block has passed all consensus-layer validation rules

nodes.label: Check Execution Payload Validity
nodes.description: Verify execution payload via execution engine (may be deferred for optimistic sync)

nodes.label: Block Propagated to Peers
nodes.description: Block is forwarded to other peers on the gossip network regardless of execution payload validity

nodes.label: Block Rejected
nodes.description: Block fails consensus-layer validation and is rejected with no propagation

edges.label: Propagate block even before execution payload verification
Optionally verify execution payload (may be deferred)

sub_graphs.title: Bellatrix: Block Request/Response Protocols
sub_graphs.description: Models the versioned request/response protocols for retrieving beacon blocks by range and by root

nodes.label: Block Request Received
nodes.description: A BeaconBlocksByRange/v2 or BeaconBlocksByRoot/v2 request has been received from a peer

nodes.label: Determine Fork Version for Response
nodes.description: Compute the fork version for each requested slot/root to determine the correct response type (phase0, altair, or bellatrix)

nodes.label: Serialize Block with Correct Type
nodes.description: Serialize the SignedBeaconBlock using the fork-appropriate SSZ schema (max chunk size 10 MiB)

nodes.label: Response Chunks Sent
nodes.description: Response chunks containing requested blocks have been sent back to the requesting peer

edges.label: Peer sends BeaconBlocksByRange/v2 or BeaconBlocksByRoot/v2 request
Resolve fork version per requested block
Select correct SSZ schema for serialization
Send serialized block chunks (up to 10 MiB each)

external_entities.name: Requesting Peer
external_entities.description: A peer node requesting blocks via the req/resp protocol

sub_graphs.title: Bellatrix: Execution Payload Peer Scoring Policy
sub_graphs.description: Models the security-critical peer scoring decisions around invalid execution payloads to prevent network segregation

nodes.label: Block with Invalid Execution Payload Detected
nodes.description: A block has been determined to have an invalid execution payload after execution engine verification

nodes.label: Evaluate Peer Scoring Decision
nodes.description: Determine whether to downscore the peer that sent the block based on invalidity type

nodes.label: No Peer Downscore Applied
nodes.description: Peer is not downscored because the invalidity is execution-layer only; prevents network segregation between optimistic and non-optimistic nodes

nodes.label: Peer Downscored or Disconnected
nodes.description: Peer is downscored/disconnected because block violates consensus-layer rules

edges.label: Invalidity is execution-layer only; no downscore to prevent segregation
Block violates consensus-layer rules; MAY downscore peer

ambiguities.text: Nodes 'should never downscore/disconnect nodes due to such invalid payloads' — the use of 'should never' is ambiguous between a strong requirement (MUST NOT) and a recommendation (SHOULD NOT).
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume this is a SHOULD NOT (RFC 2119), meaning implementations are strongly recommended not to downscore but have limited discretion. This interpretation is based on the rationale about preventing network segregation.

ambiguities.text: Message size increased to 10 MiB due to 'ExecutionPayload type can cause BeaconBlocks to exceed the 1 MiB bounds' — no precise maximum block size is specified.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume the 10 MiB limit is a hard maximum for both gossip and req/resp chunks. Blocks exceeding this are invalid at the network layer.

implicit_assumptions.description: Optimistic and non-optimistic nodes coexist on the same gossip network and must receive the same blocks to maintain consensus.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Network partition between optimistic and fully-validating nodes could lead to consensus forks or delayed finality.

implicit_assumptions.description: An attacker cannot cheaply generate blocks that pass consensus validation but have invalid execution payloads at scale, since only the block proposer can create valid-looking blocks.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: DoS vector where invalid-execution blocks flood the gossip network consuming bandwidth (up to 10 MiB each) without peer scoring consequences.
